name: Low-carbon cement and concrete
summary: Lower-clinker binders, alternative cement chemistries and carbon mineralisation reduce the emissions associated with making structural concrete.
useCase: A public project specifies a verified carbon budget per cubic metre, allowing qualified lower-clinker mixes or mineralised concrete that meets strength and durability requirements.
whyNow: Existing ready-mix infrastructure offers routes to reduce emissions without replacing the entire construction supply chain. CarbonCure’s producer network passed 50 million cumulative cubic yards in March 2024 and more than 83.6 million in November 2025, showing commercial adoption of one mineralisation approach. This is not a census of all lower-carbon concrete. Blended cement, calcined clay, alternative binders and captured-CO₂ curing have different cost, material and qualification requirements. A product marketed as low carbon can still have substantial emissions. Procurement should compare independently documented lifecycle emissions at equivalent strength, curing conditions, service life and transport distance.

mainstream.scope: Routine specification of qualified lower-carbon mixes in major infrastructure and commercial construction markets; especially lower-clinker blends and compatible mineralisation.
mainstream.rationale: Several approaches fit established concrete production and can scale through existing suppliers and procurement standards. More novel clinker-free processes may require longer qualification and financing cycles. Routine availability of some lower-carbon options before 2030 is plausible; fully eliminating cement process emissions across the world by 2035 is not assumed.

metric.name: Cumulative CarbonCure concrete produced
metric.scope: CarbonCure producer network worldwide; one mineralisation supplier, not all low-carbon concrete.
metric.limitations: Cumulative volume cannot be treated as annual output or global market share. CarbonCure’s CO₂-injection and cement-efficiency approach represents only one technology. Volume does not directly equal tonnes of emissions avoided, and the observation periods are not full calendar years.
metric.futureNote: No defensible comparable external deployment forecast found. The separate maturity path is an analyst scenario, not measured adoption.

milestones.text: CarbonCure described permanent mineralisation in its technical explanation; lower-carbon concrete was already a commercial niche.
No comparable annual all-technology production series retained; construction trials and supplier counts are not substituted for delivered volume.
No consistent annual global volume observation identified; the subsequent cumulative milestones are kept at their actual dates.
CarbonCure announced 50 million cumulative cubic yards on 6 March.
CarbonCure reported more than 83.6 million cubic yards across 10 million truckloads on 24 November.
CarbonCure’s June update described new MIT-linked research on CO₂ mineralisation and early strength; technical progress is separate from annual market output.

tailwinds: Large recurring concrete demand creates many opportunities for incremental mix improvement.
Incumbent producers and admixture suppliers can distribute qualified products through existing plants.
Carbon-aware procurement can reward verified improvement at equivalent performance.
bottlenecks: Structural approval and long-term durability matter more than a laboratory strength result alone.
Alternative feedstock availability and transport can limit local economics.
Conservative specifications, producer liability and inconsistent emissions accounting slow adoption.
watchMetrics: Annual delivered volume by certified mix and application, separated from cumulative announcements.
Verified kg CO₂-equivalent per cubic metre at equivalent performance and system boundary.
Repeat paid orders, procurement inclusion and durability evidence over realistic service conditions.
